iconicAnchor.label: William Morris interiors, furnishings, and botanical repeat patterns
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The V&A presents Arts and Crafts as a reform movement joining traditional handicraft, truthful treatment of materials, domestic design, and the social relationship between designing and making.

sources.title: Arts and Crafts: an introduction
supports: Arts and Crafts was structured by ideals of handicraft, material understanding, and improved design for ordinary domestic objects.
The movement worked across buildings, workshops, furniture, and applied arts rather than as a single ornamental motif.

sources.title: William Morris and wallpaper design
supports: Morris built repeat patterns from closely observed plant forms that were stylized and ordered rather than copied literally.
His wallpapers used hand-cut woodblocks and natural mineral-based dyes, connecting visible print process to the finished surface.
